refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: These files configure systemd-device-accept-d.service8, which applies the device acceptance configuration from accept.d5. See systemd.syntax7 for a general description of the syntax.

refsect1.title: [DeviceAccept] Section Options
refsect1.para: The following options are available in the [DeviceAccept] section:

listitem.para: Takes a whitespace-separated list of bus names, such as pci. While the service runs, the kernel does not probe drivers for the devices on these buses on its own: neither for devices that are added, nor for devices without a driver when a driver for them is loaded. This is achieved by writing 0 to the drivers_autoprobe attribute of the bus, for example /sys/bus/pci/drivers_autoprobe. Instead, the service binds drivers to these devices once it has applied the configuration from accept.d5 to them. This way, the trust policy of a device is in place before a driver is probed for it, also for devices that are added while the system runs, regardless of whether their driver is loaded already. Driver probing is only held while there is acceptance configuration, i.e. while at least one valid file in accept.d/ exists. Without any, the default policy of the kernel applies.

A device on one of these buses that a file selects goes through the acceptance flow described in systemd-device-accept-d.service8 first, which applies its requested policy through trust_policy, and a driver is only bound to it if the policy could be applied and is not disabled. A device that no file selects gets a driver right away. Devices without a matching driver are retried when a driver is registered on their bus or another device is bound. Deferred probes are also retried periodically. After a driver is explicitly unbound, probing waits for a new driver registration on that bus or a configuration reload, which restarts the acceptance flow.

A failed or deferred probe can make trust_policy immutable even though the device has no driver. Reloading the configuration retries unbound devices, but can only change their policy if the kernel has not started matching or probing a driver for them. Unbinding a driver does not make the policy writable again.

A bus that does not exist when the service is started, because the module that provides it is not loaded yet, is held after its registration is observed. This is also done when a bus is removed and registered again. Devices may be probed before the registration event is processed. Before a bus is held, and before the service is started, drivers are probed as usual, which in particular applies to the drivers built into the kernel during boot. When the service is stopped, which includes switching from the initrd to the root file system, the drivers_autoprobe attribute of these buses is set back to the value it had before the service turned probing off, until the service is started again. The original value is kept in /run/systemd/device-accept/, so that it is restored also if the service has been restarted in between, for example after a crash. Devices that were not bound to a driver at that point are probed by the kernel only when a driver for them is loaded afterwards, and only if automatic probing was turned on originally.

Note that some kernel subsystems bind drivers to devices directly, regardless of this setting, and so does writing to the bind attribute of a driver. Also note that the sriov_drivers_autoprobe attribute of a PCI device is not a replacement for this setting: it only makes the probing of the drivers for the virtual functions of the device fail, which means that their trust policy cannot be changed anymore afterwards.

This option may be specified more than once, in which case the buses are added to the list. If an empty string is assigned, the list is reset. Defaults to empty, i.e. driver probing is left to the kernel.
